hints: Notice the resistive force is given as $kv^2$, not a constant, so the force grows with speed $v$.
At maximum speed on a horizontal road there is no acceleration, so driving force $F$ equals resistive force $kv^2$.
Use $P = Fv$ with $F = kv^2$ and rearrange $P = kv^3$ to find the relation for $v$.
walkthrough: Identify the condition for maximum speed: on a horizontal road at constant maximum $v$, resultant force is zero, so forward driving force $F$ equals total resistive force $kv^2$.
Recall the power relation for a force moving at speed $v$: $P = Fv$.
Substitute $F = kv^2$ into the power equation: $P = (kv^2) \times v = kv^3$.
Rearrange for the speed term by dividing both sides by $k$: $v^3 = P/k$.

options.A: At top speed $P = Fv = kv^2 \times v = kv^3$, so $v^3 = P/k$.
options.B: This omits one factor of $v$ by setting $P$ equal to the force $kv^2$ instead of $Fv$.
options.C: Squaring $P/k$ does not follow from $P = kv^3$ and gives the wrong power of $v$.
options.D: Cubing $P/k$ does not follow from $P = kv^3$; $v$ is proportional to the cube root of $P/k$.
